withdrawn_scenes.title: Where the outlier fence sits
withdrawn_scenes.purpose: See the interquartile range as the width of the box and the outlier boundary as a fence measured from the upper quartile.

steps.text: The box runs from $Q_1=11$ to $Q_3=21$, so its width is the interquartile range, $21-11=10$. This is the first B1.
With $m=1.5$ the upper fence starts at the upper quartile: $21+1.5\times 10=36$. The whisker ends at $33$, inside the fence, and $44$ is beyond it. This is the second B1.

Drag $m$ to $1$: the fence moves to $31$. That is the slip of adding only one IQR, and it would wrongly put the whisker end of $33$ outside the fence. The lower fence $11-15=-4$ is below every reading, so there are no low outliers.

legend.meaning: The single reading plotted on its own as an outlier, at $44$ mg per litre.

The box, running from the lower quartile to the upper quartile, with the median line inside it.

interact.watch: The upper fence slides right as $m$ grows and left as it shrinks. At $m=1.5$ it sits at $36$: the whisker end is inside it and the point $44$ is beyond it. Lower values of $m$ show how using the wrong multiple would misplace the fence.

question_link.text: The green bar is the interquartile range asked for in (i), giving $10$ mg per litre for the first B1. The fence at $m=1.5$ is the boundary asked for in (ii), $Q_3+1.5\times 10=36$, for the second B1.

read_off: The on-screen text restates the interquartile range and the upper boundary as $Q_3+m\times 10$; it updates with the slider, and at the trust's rule it gives $36$ mg per litre.

withdrawn_scenes.title: Taking the same amount off every reading
withdrawn_scenes.purpose: See that subtracting a constant slides the whole box plot left without changing the width of the box.

steps.text: At $s=0$ the box is the original one, with quartiles $11$ and $21$ and IQR $10$.
Drag $s$ to $1.5$: the quartiles become $9.5$ and $19.5$, so the IQR is $19.5-9.5=10$. This is the B1 for the value $10$.
Both quartiles slide left by the same amount, so the box keeps its width. A shift changes the location, not the spread, so the IQR stays $10$, not $8.5$. This is the dB1 for the reason.
